report.question: Can a workflow parameter value containing shell metacharacters, an apostrophe, a here-string terminator, a newline or a PowerShell escape caret alter the command a shell adapter executes?
report.answer: YES on STRING-COMMAND / HERE-STRING / unquoted-IEX adapters on this Linux host (canary file created: A3, A3B, A4, A7, A9B). NO on ARGV-ARRAY adapters A1/A2/A5/A8 (ArgumentList, python list, POSIX $@, PowerShell native call): metacharacters are inert and argv is intact. A9 quoted IEX is PARTIAL (argv divergence, no canary). A6 arithmetic-eval is NOT-CHECKED for argv (no sleeper) and canary-silent under set -u on this host. Safety of argv adapters must not be cited as safety of string-command adapters. A5 is SAFE here; the prior Windows git-bash MSYS /sdcard rewrite does not apply on Linux.
named_probes_verbatim: Probe 1: drive each adapter with the corpus and detect execution divergence via a canary side effect (a file the injected fragment would create) rather than by reading stdout.

Probe 2 (mechanically different): capture the actual child process command line from the OS process table and compare it to the intended argv - a value that reaches the child unchanged is safe even if stdout looks odd, and a value that alters argv is unsafe even if no canary fired.

argv-array adapters and string-command adapters must be reported separately; a program that is safe only because one adapter happens to use argv must say so
